A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Mustafar and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C. Retained material can be matched reliably across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original LongBench evaluations, pruning comparisons, compression measurements, and inference-throughput experiments, including additional experiments in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds RULER accuracy results and measurements of time to first token and generation throughput.

M1.justification: Per-token magnitude pruning, the dense local window, bitmap compression, and sparse attention computation remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 explicitly documents the existing attention procedure; attribution to Coruscant does not establish a changed implementation.

E1.justification: v2 adds RULER evaluation at 65,536-token context length, covering single- and multiple-needle retrieval, variable tracking, frequent-word extraction, and question answering (Appendix A.3, Table 11). This substantially extends long-context task coverage beyond the retained LongBench evaluations.

E2.justification: The existing comparison methods remain, including dense inference, ThinK, pruning variants, and 2:4 sparsity. RULER extends the dense/ThinK comparison to another benchmark. Identifying FlashAttention as the existing dense throughput baseline is additional disclosure, without evidence of a comparator replacement.

E3.justification: The added evaluations introduce Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct at 65,536 tokens and a batch-size-4 timing study with 512, 1024, and 2048 generated tokens. Appendix C.3 adds time to first token and generated-token throughput over end-to-end duration, substantially expanding latency accounting beyond retained Figure 7.

E4.justification: Appendix C.3 adds an output-length sensitivity study examining whether decoding gains compensate for pruning and compression overhead. Earlier pruning ablations, larger-model evaluation, higher-sparsity tests, and semi-structured comparisons remain; the higher-sparsity section merely moves from A.3 to A.4.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed or repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or error bars. The added tables continue reporting point estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 11 and 14 add substantial accuracy and timing results. For example, Table 14 reports Llama-3 throughput of 89.699 versus dense 59.242 tokens/s for 2048 generated tokens at joint 70% sparsity, alongside slower first-token latency of 3.151 versus 2.769 seconds. Table 4 also corrects the Mistral joint-50% average from 54.15 to 42.30, matching unchanged Table 3.

T1.justification: The pruning-score formulas and reasoning about per-token Value pruning remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 expresses the previously described attention computation explicitly; it adds no new theoretical result, assumption, proof, or substantive derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims about accuracy-preserving unstructured KV pruning, sparsity up to 70%, cache size reaching 45% of dense storage, and throughput gains up to 2.23×. Additional experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: Appendix C.3 newly discusses increased first-token latency and its compensation through faster decoding. Appendix A.3 interprets RULER performance as evidence of versatility across tasks. The conclusion also adds future combinations with weight and activation sparsity while retaining the per-head/per-layer sparsity limitation.

D1.justification: v2 identifies FlashAttention as the dense baseline implementation for both prefill and decode, and clarifies that Figure 7 throughput counts input and output tokens. Algorithm 1 makes the retained computation more explicit. The code access information, hardware disclosure, and cache-tiling details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 3 now attributes the bitmap format to Coruscant and describes Mustafar as extending it. v2 also adds RULER, MagicPIG, and weight/activation-sparsity references supporting evaluation and future work. The broader research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized grammar and terminology edits, reorganizes the kernel explanation, adds pseudocode and funding acknowledgments, and adjusts appendix subsection organization. The main narrative and section sequence remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v2 revises labels and illustrations in Figures 1, 3, and 4, reverses and relabels Figure 5's panels, and adds Algorithm 1 and two results tables. Existing tables and figures undergo limited relocation while retaining the overall visual format.

improvement.justification: The RULER evaluation and explicit first-token/end-to-end timing strengthen validation and expose a latency tradeoff missing from v1. Clearer algorithm and baseline documentation, Coruscant attribution, and the corrected Mistral average improve transparency and reliability. These are incremental gains; the blanket RULER accuracy-preservation interpretation remains stronger than Table 11 supports, including variable-tracking accuracy of 0.869 versus dense 0.973 at joint 70% sparsity.
